index.html.142: Before each request, the lab checks key usage reported by OpenRouter. The daily limit resets at midnight UTC. This is a monitoring limit and pending or concurrent requests may exceed it. Set a hard limit in OpenRouter. Both limits include usage outside the lab and before the key was added. The total may restart when the key is replaced. Leave a field blank to disable its monitoring limit.
index.html.143: The input price may not exceed the same limit. Zero allows free dialogue models only, while JEV, context compaction and the jury remain funded by the sponsor key. These limits apply within the lab. Also set the overall key budget in OpenRouter.
index.html.145: The key is linked to the signed-in LinkedIn account. The sponsor name, account holder and funding attribution are displayed publicly. Sponsors cannot view the private conversations they fund. The server stores the key encrypted. You may replace it, change its limits, or delete it. Requests already sent to the provider are not canceled, and editing a key does not reset daily quotas.
index.html.150: The harness runs the model and manages its memory. The lab supplies tasks and evaluates responses. It cannot verify the actual reasoning setting used externally.

privacy.html.7: PrisonLab is a community laboratory for comparing the performance of AI models across fictional cases and characters. This page explains the data used in experiments, what is shown to visitors, and the role of external services.
privacy.html.9: Login is required to start experiments. Your conversations are private by default, and posting and sharing to LinkedIn are optional, independent steps.
privacy.html.11: The lab stores conversation text, model and character choices, simulated emotions, jury reports, reviews you write, and usage and cost information returned by providers. This data is used to complete the session and evaluate models. Emotions belong to the fictional character and are not a psychological diagnosis of the user.
privacy.html.12: Your records are linked to your LinkedIn account ID, and you can access them when you sign in with the same account from another browser. Old records created before accounts were linked are not automatically attributed to any new account.
privacy.html.14: The conversation only appears in the public gallery when you choose to publish it after its evaluation is complete. Upon publication, its text, results, sentiment, reviews and available usage data become viewable via a public link. Review the content before publishing, and avoid entering other people's personal information, secrets, or data into experiments.
privacy.html.15: The public profile displays only posted conversations, with the account holder's name and photo as a participant or simulation player, and their associated reviews, if any. Ranking lists do not display private conversations. The estimated ranking before publishing appears to the owner of the conversation, and changes when other results are added.
privacy.html.17: We request only sign-in and basic profile permissions (
privacy.html.18: ): the account identifier for this application, name and photo when available. We do not request your LinkedIn password, email address, or connections. The server uses the LinkedIn response to sign you in and discards the access tokens. We do not store them in your account or conversations. LinkedIn sign-in does not verify a person’s real identity.
privacy.html.19: We save a derived internal account ID, a random public ID, name and photo link, and the dates the account was created and updated. The purpose is to link records to the account, apply a daily limit, and show who has posted conversations. You can request deletion of account data via the contact link below.
privacy.html.21: The Share button is available only for published conversations. It opens the LinkedIn composer with the public link so that you can review the post and choose the audience and whether to publish. The lab does not post automatically or request posting permission during sign-in. Enabling the Share on LinkedIn product does not automatically authorize the site to post on your behalf.
privacy.html.23: The default site-funded allowance is three new conversations per account per day. A sponsor can change the limits on their key. The daily quota resets at midnight Jerusalem time. Starting a conversation consumes one test even if you stop or delete it. Your own key allows unlimited new site tests, subject to your provider’s balance and limits. A conversation retains its original funding source and a personally funded conversation requires the same key when resumed.
privacy.html.24: The conversation shows the amount reported by the provider and identifies site or personal-key funding. Visitors can see this information when the conversation is published. The cost may be partial when a provider does not report some calls. Key balance and OpenRouter account information are available only to the key holder. An unavailable balance does not mean it is zero or unlimited.
privacy.html.26: Case instructions, character profiles, and the necessary conversation content are sent to OpenRouter and selected model providers, including those used for emotions, judging, and context compaction. These providers apply their own data processing and retention policies. Do not send login credentials to chat models.
privacy.html.27: If you enter your OpenRouter key, the browser saves it in
privacy.html.28: and sends it to the lab server to execute requests and check the balance through OpenRouter. The key itself is not stored in conversation files or shown to visitors. We store a derived fingerprint to bind a resumed conversation to its funding source, and exclude that fingerprint from interface responses. Signing out removes the key from browser storage. The site key remains on the server.
privacy.html.32: A LinkedIn account holder can add a sponsor OpenRouter key under a person or organization name, with the linked account holder displayed. Saving a sponsorship consents to displaying the sponsor name, owner and limits to visitors and using the key within the specified limits. The server encrypts sponsor keys in private JSON outside the public site, with a separate encryption key and restricted permissions. We do not reveal the key or fingerprint to visitors or put them in conversation files, the code repository or deployment backups.
privacy.html.33: Each sponsor has a separate daily quota per LinkedIn account and a maximum dialogue-model price per million tokens. A zero limit allows only free dialogue models while the same sponsor funds JEV, compaction and judging. Lab limits do not change the key budget in OpenRouter. Creating a test consumes quota. Deleting it, replacing the key or changing limits does not reset the quota.
privacy.html.34: The key owner may replace, disable, limit or delete it. Changes affect subsequent calls and cannot cancel a request already sent to the provider. The conversation stays bound to its original sponsor. We do not automatically charge the site key or another sponsor if that key is disabled. The saved sponsor name and funding attribution remain visible with previously published conversations. Deleting the key does not delete other people’s conversations. Sponsors cannot see private conversation content or the identities of users who consumed quota through the sponsorship panel.
privacy.html.35: Links to cases, investigator characters, models, rankings and public profiles can be shared. Public profile tabs show published tests where the account holder was the investigator, accused or operator of an AI-versus-AI simulation. A link does not grant access to a private conversation. Deleted or unpublished conversations are not visible to visitors.
privacy.html.37: We record the success and failure of model calls, response time, and generation rate to illustrate their reliability. These measurements do not guarantee future response of the model. The site uses a cookie for session and request protection, and its interface uses Google Fonts that your browser may connect to. Website hosting may maintain operational and security logs such as request time and network address.
privacy.html.39: Application data is stored in private server space outside the public site and source repository. You can permanently delete any conversation you own from your account history, including published conversations. This removes its text, ratings, associated reviews and appearance in the gallery, public profile and leaderboard. The daily quota counter is retained without conversation content to prevent quota reuse by deletion. Aggregated model performance measurements that contain neither account identity nor conversation text are also retained. Profiles remain until deletion is requested through the contact link.
privacy.html.40: Account and conversation data are excluded from code deployment backups. After deletion the conversation link is unavailable from the server. Copies or previews may remain with visitors, LinkedIn or model providers under their policies. Deleting a conversation in the lab does not delete your LinkedIn post, which you can manage there.
privacy.html.41: Do not include conversations or API keys in the public source repository. The code license does not make user data open source.
privacy.html.43: For inquiries and privacy requests, contact the site operator via
privacy.html.45: . Changes affecting data collection or publication on the site are announced before taking effect. Do not send passwords or API keys in a contact request.
privacy.html.46: PrisonLab is an independent project, and does not represent LinkedIn or the model companies used.
